title: Depth-texture fog pass with linearized depth
purpose: Fog a rendered three.js frame from its DepthTexture: turn depth values back into view distance for perspective or orthographic cameras and mix toward a fog colour with exponential squared fog after a start distance, as a ShaderPass definition or ShaderMaterial, with CPU mirrors of the depth mapping and the fog.

engine.name: webgl2_browser
engine.notes: three.js r155 or later passed in as THREE (DepthTexture on a render target, an int uniform and the colorspace_fragment chunk); only 0.186.1 was run.

contract.language: ECMAScript 2020 module; GLSL ES 3.00 through three.js ShaderMaterial

exports.summary: A fresh shader definition with tDiffuse, tDepth, cameraNear and cameraFar for ShaderPass or ShaderMaterial.

exports.name: createDepthFogMaterial
exports.summary: The definition as a full-screen ShaderMaterial without depth test or write.

exports.name: linearizeDepth
exports.signature: linearizeDepth(depth, near, far, orthographic = false) -> number
exports.summary: CPU mirror: view distance for a [0, 1] depth-buffer value.

options.name: start
options.meaning: View distance where the fog begins.

options.name: orthographic
options.meaning: The depth buffer comes from an orthographic camera (linear depth).

limits: Fog is uniform in space and follows planar view depth (distance along the camera axis), as three.js's own fog does, not radial distance, height or noise; light does not scatter through it. The background (depth 1) is fogged as if it sat at the far plane. Assumes the WebGL default depth range: logarithmic depth buffers and reversed depth are not supported. cameraNear and cameraFar must match the camera that rendered the depth, and transparent objects that do not write depth are fogged by what lies behind them. Output goes through three.js's output colour space conversion. Only three.js 0.186.1 was run, in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2.
technique_references: Inverting the perspective depth mapping: d = far (z - near) / (z (far - near))
